templates.pattern: [P1] starts from O, walks [D1] km North to A, then [D2] km East to B, then [D3] km South to C, then [D4] km West to D, then [D5] km North to E. What is the straight-line distance from O to E?
[P1] goes [D1] km East, turns left, goes [D2] km, turns left, goes [D3] km, turns right, goes [D4] km, turns right, goes [D5] km. In which direction is [P1] from start?
templates.explanation: E[D1]→N[D2]→W[D3]→N[D4]→E[D5]. Net E=[D1-D3+D5], Net N=[D2+D4]. Both positive → North-East.

templates.pattern: [P1] starts from village A and walks [D1] km South to B, [D2] km West to C, [D3] km North to D, [D4] km East to E, [D5] km North to F. What is the direction of F from A and distance?
templates.explanation: Net N=[D3-D1+D5], Net E=[D4-D2]. If both positive → NE. Distance=√(Net_N²+Net_E²)

templates.pattern: [P1],[P2],[P3] start from point O at the same time. [P1] goes [D1] km North. [P2] goes [D1] km East. [P3] goes [D1] km South-West (45°). After reaching their points, [P1] turns and walks to [P2]'s position. How far does [P1] walk?
templates.explanation: [P1] at N[D1], [P2] at E[D1]. Distance between them = √([D1]²+[D1]²) = [D1]√2

templates.pattern: [P1] is at the centre of a circular park. He walks [D1] m North, [D1] m East, [D1] m South, [D1] m West, [D1] m North, [D1] m East. What is his final displacement from centre?
templates.explanation: N[D1]+E[D1]+S[D1]+W[D1] cancel each other. Then N[D1]+E[D1] remain. Net = √([D1]²+[D1]²) = [D1]√2 in NE direction.

templates.pattern: Town X is [D1] km North of town Y. Town Z is [D2] km East of Y. Town W is [D3] km South of Z. Town V is [D4] km West of W. What is the direction of V from X?
templates.explanation: Y at origin. X at N[D1]. Z at E[D2]. W at E[D2]+S[D3]. V at E[D2-D4]+S[D3]. V relative to X: E[D2-D4] and S[D1+D3]. Direction from X to V is South-East.

templates.pattern: [P1] walks from A: [D1] km East, [D2] km North, [D3] km East, [D4] km South, [D5] km West. What is the shortest distance from the final point back to A?
[P1] walks from home: [D1] km West to A, [D2] km North to B, [D3] km East to C, [D2] km South to D, [D4] km East to E. How far is E from home and in which direction?
templates.explanation: W[D1]+N[D2]+E[D3]+S[D2]+E[D4]. N-S cancel. Net E=[D3+D4-D1]. East of home.

templates.pattern: [P1] and [P2] start from O. [P1] goes [D1] km North and [D2] km East. [P2] goes [D3] km West and [D4] km North. [P3] is at the midpoint of [P1] and [P2]. What is [P3]'s distance from O?
A ship sails [D1] km North, then [D2] km East, then [D3] km South-East (45°). What is the total Eastward displacement from start? (SE East component = [D3]/√2)
A train goes [D1] km East, [D2] km North-East (45°), [D3] km North. What is the total displacement from start? (NE components: N=[D2]/√2, E=[D2]/√2)

[P1] is standing at junction J. Going [D1] km North leads to school S. Going [D2] km East from S leads to hospital H. Going [D3] km South from H leads to market M. [P2] goes directly from J to M. In which direction does [P2] go and how far?
templates.explanation: M is at E[D2]+S[D3-D1] from J (since D3>D1). Direction = South-East. Distance=√([D2]²+([D3-D1])²)

templates.pattern: [P1] walks [D1] km South, [D2] km West, [D3] km North, [D4] km East, [D5] km South, [D6] km West. What is the final displacement and direction from start?
templates.explanation: Net S=[D1+D5-D3]. Net W=[D2+D6-D4]. Direction=South-West. Distance=√(Net_S²+Net_W²)
